conviction_note: Every live input (the July guide of a high-single-digit Q1 margin, the $0.28 bar that the guide implies, the diesel spike, UBS's 'tracked trends remain weak', GIS reaffirming on 09-23) is in the wire and in a 13% September drawdown. The one company-specific item I found, continuing IEEPA tariff refunds after $6m in Q4, is a small one-off on a name whose beats have been sold. LESSONS.md rule 2 took it from +0.3 to dropped, so the honest answer is 0.
bar: Q1 FY27 adjusted EPS $0.28 on revenue $2.59B. Two sources agree: Investing.com 2026-09-29 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/conagra-earnings-on-deck-as-freight-costs-test-lowbar-guidance-93CH-4922902) and TradingView (https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:3bd3b386e78b9:0-cag-q1-26-earnings-eps-estimate-is-0-28-usd/). The $0.28 fits the company's own Q1 guide of a 'high single digits' adjusted operating margin (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/22/conagra-cag-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/): about 9% on $2.59B is roughly $0.28. Zacks carries $0.31 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/insights-conagra-brands-cag-q1-121513361.html, 2026-09-25), but its segment operating profits sum to about a 10% margin, above the guide, so I treat it as the outlier. The name trades on the FY27 guide ($1.40-1.50 adjusted EPS, organic sales -3% to -1%, margin 10.0-10.5%), not on the quarter.
positioning_check: Short interest 8.48% of float, 4.86 days to cover, 40.3m shares (Fintel, settlement 2026-09-15, https://fintel.io/ss/us/cag, from the sweep row; not independently re-verified). That is not crowded. The 25-delta skew is +0.59 vol points, i.e. balanced, and the put/call OI ratio is 0.7. The options market makes no directional statement. It prices a 4.76% event move against a 2.05% median own reaction, so the vol is rich relative to history.
searched_and_found_nothing: IEEPA tariff refunds. The Q4 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023217/000002321726000022/tmb-20260715xex99d1.htm) records $6m of tariff refunds booked in productivity. The Q1 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23217/000002321725000083/tmb-20251001xex99d1.htm) shows a 30% tariff on selected China imports, which is IEEPA and refundable after the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling. More refunds could therefore land in Q1, but no Q1 amount is sourced, the steel-can tariffs under Section 232 are not refundable, and a refund is a one-off on a name that sells beats. Drafted at +0.3, then dropped (see lessons_applied).

Diesel and freight. Diesel averaged $6.53/gal in August 2026 and hit records in September. Reefer surcharges were up 10c m/m and spot linehaul was more than 30% above a year earlier (DAT, 2026-09-15, https://www.dat.com/company/news-events/news-releases/dat-spot-van-rate-falls-20-cents-in-steepest-august-pullback-on-record). That is a real risk to the FY27 guide, but RBC and UBS have flagged it by name (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/ubs-maintains-neutral-on-conagra-stock-amid-cost-pressures-93CH-4913400) and the stock fell 13% in September. The company has not quantified its own exposure, and I could not read the energy-hedge disclosure because the 10-K fetch was truncated. It is a macro-to-company hypothesis and it is priced.

Peer prints since Conagra's July call. General Mills 2026-09-23: organic sales flat, NA Retail -3%, FY reaffirmed, stock -1% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040704/000162828026063141/a20260923ex99.htm). Smucker 2026-08-26: FY raised, including a tariff refund. Campbell's 2026-09-03: FY27 guided 9% below consensus. The read-through is mixed and public, and CAG kept falling after the GIS print.

EDGAR 8-Ks since 2026-07-15. A $500m 5.40% note due 2031 (07-28): refinancing, no distress read. COO McGough retiring and the role eliminated (07-28 filing). Director Chirico not standing again, no disagreement stated (06-23). AGM results (09-28): say-on-pay passed only 146.9m to 142.5m, and a shareholder proposal restricting blank-check preferred passed 178.7m to 110.9m. That is governance discontent, but it has no dated catalyst in or after the window and I found no 2026 activist stake.
Form 4s. The CEO bought 35,000 shares at $14.59 on 2026-07-17 (public, widely covered), and directors bought in April 2026. Since then only a deferred-comp grant at $16.11 on 09-01. No new cluster.
Scanner data (Circana/Nielsen) for Jun-Aug 2026. No company-level takeaway numbers found beyond UBS's 'tracked trends remain weak', which is in the wire.
Recalls, plant closures and divestitures since July. Nothing new: the Chef Boyardee and frozen-fish sales closed in Q1 FY26 and are in organic adjustments.
baseline_tension: Nothing I found cuts against the baseline. The skew is balanced, the stock is already down 12.4% over 20 days and 30% off its high on exactly the freight and inflation fears the Street has written up, and consensus sits where the company's own Q1 margin guide puts it, so the price already holds what I found.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (size one-offs as one-offs; the tariff-refund thesis was right and noise on four names, split by guide direction) and rule 5 (transmission is a hypothesis until the company says it): the draft's only finding, continuing IEEPA refunds in Q1 (+0.3, lands_on one_off), has no Q1 amount from the company and no path to the guide. On a name that fell after its last beat, it was dropped. That takes the sum from 0.3 to 0 and expected_move_pct from 0.2 to 0.

Rule 1 (the reaction function vetoes the fundamental read): print_vs_bar_pct stays at +2.0, a slight EPS beat against a guide-derived $0.28 bar in line with the average trailing surprise. expected_move_pct is 0 because 5 of the last 7 reactions were down and the July beat was sold on the guide.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar was already sourced to two agreeing estimates plus the company guide, so nothing changed there.
